figure_caption: Overview. A public score matrix, an investment model (independent non-negative per-task gains with L1 or L0 cost), and an aggregation rule define an instance in which a target model must become strictly first. A planner proposes a gain plan; a trusted verifier recomputes the rule on the modified matrix; efficiency is the cost of the evaluator's reference plan divided by the cost of the verified plan, capped at 2.

panels.title: Instance, planner, verifier and efficiency
panels.short_caption: Instance (matrix, investment model, eight rules) feeds a verification-first planner; a trusted verifier and reference solver define capped efficiency.
panels.drawio_prompt:
SINGLE IDEA: one left-to-right pipeline showing how a targeted-investment instance (score matrix + investment model + aggregation rule) is solved by a verification-first planner, re-checked by a trusted evaluator, and scored as efficiency against a reference solver. Full-width, wide (about 21:9) canvas; three labelled zones side by side plus a scoring strip at the right end.

ZONE A — 'Instance' (left, about 32% of width; three stacked groups):
- A_matrix (sharp-cornered data grid, N rows x T columns, with row/column ticks 'models' and 'tasks'; title 'Score matrix X'): one row is the TARGET row, drawn as the most prominent row and tagged 'target i'. All other rows are plain data rows.
- A_gain (sharp data strip, T cells, aligned under the matrix columns, title 'Gains g ≥ 0'): feeds the target row only. A_plus (⊕ node) sits on the target row: incoming edge from the matrix target row labelled '$$x_i$$', incoming edge from A_gain labelled '$$g$$'; outgoing edge to the modified matrix. Other rows carry a small 'unchanged' tag. A_cap: small tag on A_gain reading 'per-task caps'.
- A_cost (two small side-by-side rounded boxes titled 'Cost'): 'L1 points' (glyph: Σ over bar cells) and 'L0 tasks touched' (glyph: count of non-zero cells). Both attach to A_gain with dashed edges (auxiliary).
- A_rules (a grouped region titled 'Aggregation rule r', containing eight rounded chips in two sub-groups): sub-group 'Score levels' = mean, median, trimmed mean, z-score mean, maximin; sub-group 'Orderings' = Borda, plurality, Copeland. Each chip carries a small solver-type badge: 'exact' on mean, median, maximin, plurality; 'heuristic' on trimmed mean, z-score mean, Borda, Copeland. A tiny legend for the two badges.
- A_goal (rounded box): 'Target strictly first'. Edge from A_rules and from A_plus' modified matrix into A_goal (solid).

ZONE B — 'Verification-first planner' (centre, about 36% of width; one large grouped region containing five numbered steps):
- B1 (rounded box) 'Feasibility screens' -> B2 (rounded box) 'Per-rule candidate plans' -> B3 (rounded box) 'Verify and prune' -> B4 (rounded box) 'Boundary polish' -> B_out (small sharp box) 'Gain plan g'. Steps run left-to-right/top-to-bottom as a compact snake of at most two rows, solid edges. B1 has two small exits: 'already first → empty plan' and 'full-cap fails → infeasible', both going directly to B_out via thin solid edges.
- B2 contains three small stacked tags: 'Exact solver', 'Verified heuristic', 'Uniform fill'. All three feed B3.
- B_replica (cylinder-free small rounded box inside B3, titled 'Exact rule replica'): B3 consults it; dashed edge B3 ↔ B_replica. B4 loops back to B3 with a dashed edge labelled 'verify'.
- B_fb (small rounded box) 'Fallback: uniform / headroom fill', reached by a dashed edge labelled 'error' from the planner group border; it feeds B_out.
- Edges from Zone A: A_goal → B1 and A_plus (modified instance) → B1, solid. These are the planner's inputs.

ZONE C — 'Trusted evaluator' (right, about 32% of width):
- C_ver (rounded box) 'Trusted verifier' with a sub-line chip 'recomputes rule on X + gains'. Edge B_out → C_ver (solid, label '$$g$$'). Output: decision diamond C_ok 'Strictly first?' (ties count against).
- C_ref (rounded box) 'Reference solver' (small tag 'exact or search'), fed from the instance with a long solid edge from Zone A (route it along the bottom edge of the canvas), producing 'ref cost'. Next to it small sharp box 'Naive baselines' attached by a dashed edge (comparison only).
- C_div (÷ node): incoming edge from C_ref labelled 'ref cost'; incoming edge from C_ok (yes branch) labelled 'plan cost'. Outgoing edge to C_cap (small clamp node 'cap 2').
- C_eff (prominent sharp result box, the most important element in the figure): 'Efficiency' with the single permitted equation riding beside it: $$\min\{2,\ \mathrm{ref}/\mathrm{cost}\}$$. Edge C_cap → C_eff.
- Outcome score strip under C_eff (three small sharp tags attached to C_eff or to the C_ok branches): 'verified, cheaper than ref → above 1', 'matches ref → 1', 'correct infeasible / empty plan → 1', 'malformed, failed verify, timeout → 0'. The 'no' branch of C_ok goes to the '0' tag with a dashed edge.
- Optional tiny annotation near C_eff: '>1 means cheaper than reference'.

EDGE SUMMARY (source → target, style, label): A_matrix target row → A_plus (solid, '$$x_i$$'); A_gain → A_plus (solid, '$$g$$'); A_cost → A_gain (dashed); A_rules → A_goal (solid); A_plus → A_goal (solid); A_goal → B1 (solid); B1 → B2 → B3 → B4 → B_out (solid); B4 → B3 (dashed, 'verify'); planner border → B_fb (dashed, 'error'); B_fb → B_out (solid); B_out → C_ver (solid, '$$g$$'); C_ver → C_ok (solid); C_ok → C_div (solid, 'plan cost'); instance → C_ref (solid, long bottom route); C_ref → C_div (solid, 'ref cost'); C_div → C_cap → C_eff (solid); C_ok no-branch → '0' tag (dashed, 'no'); B_out ... naive baselines (not connected; baselines only attach to C_ref by dashed edge).

SPATIAL LAYOUT: Zone A at left, Zone B centre, Zone C right, flow strictly left-to-right with minimal crossings; Zone C_ref sits in the lower part of Zone C, C_ver / C_ok in the upper part; the long A→C_ref edge runs along the bottom margin beneath Zone B. Align A_matrix, B1 and C_ver along a common upper band; A_rules, B_fb and C_ref along a lower band. Zone headings are bold titles above each group; groups are enclosed by light group boundaries.

IMPORTANCE RANKING: (1) C_eff 'Efficiency' and its ÷ / cap-2 construction; (2) the target row with the ⊕ gain node and the L1/L0 cost chips; (3) the planner chain B1–B4 with 'Verify and prune' and 'Exact rule replica'; (4) the eight rule chips with exact/heuristic badges; (5) Trusted verifier and Reference solver; (6) everything else (fallback, baselines, outcome tags) is secondary.
